meta_description: Genomic pipeline platform on hybrid cloud — cost per genome down 44% and turnaround from nine days to three

blocks.x: Genomic pipeline platform on hybrid cloud — cost per genome down 44% and turnaround from nine days to three

Identity withheld — a genomics lab whose sequencing machines outran its compute: samples queued for days while the on-prem cluster churned, and clinical reports waited on batch windows. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline month priced the queue: nine days median sample-to-report, EUR 214 compute cost per genome, and secondary analysis capacity fixed by hardware procurement cycles.
Clinical demand was spiky — oncology panels arrived in bursts — and the cluster sized for average load failed both directions: idle most days, overrun on burst days.

We rebuilt the pipeline as a hybrid platform: burstable secondary analysis on cloud with data gravity respected — sequencing data staged once, cached hot — workload manager scheduling across both estates, and the clinical report chain kept inside the lab's validated boundary. Cost guards run in the platform: every workload carries its budget, and overrun is a governed exception.
